title: Daily Devotional #4
paragraphs: As I read through Matthew Chapter 4, I am reminded of the temptations that Jesus faced while He was here on earth. Satan tried to lure Jesus away from His mission and purpose, but Jesus was steadfast in His faith and trust in You.

The first temptation that Satan presented to Jesus was to turn stones into bread. Satan wanted to tempt Jesus to use His divine power for His own personal gain. But Jesus knew that His mission was not to satisfy His own hunger but to fulfill the will of God. Jesus responded to Satan with the words, "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God." (Matthew 4:4).

The second temptation that Satan presented to Jesus was to throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the temple, so that the angels would rescue Him. Satan wanted to tempt Jesus to test God's protection and power. But again, Jesus knew that His mission was not to put God to the test but to trust in His goodness and sovereignty. Jesus responded to Satan with the words, "You shall not put the Lord your God to the test." (Matthew 4:7).

The third temptation that Satan presented to Jesus was to worship him in exchange for all the kingdoms of the world. Satan wanted to tempt Jesus to abandon His mission and purpose in exchange for temporary power and glory. But Jesus knew that His mission was not to seek earthly power and glory but to serve and worship God alone. Jesus responded to Satan with the words, "Be gone, Satan! For it is written, 'You shall worship the Lord your God and him only shall you serve.'" (Matthew 4:10).

As I reflect on these temptations, I am reminded of the importance of staying focused on Your will and purpose for my life. The world may offer temporary pleasures and satisfaction, but true fulfillment and joy can only be found in You. Help me to trust in Your goodness and sovereignty, and to resist the temptations of the evil one. May my life be a reflection of Your love and grace, and may I seek to serve and worship You alone.
